content.thinking: הגעתי לסעיף קרן ההשתלמות: אפשר למשוך בפטור ממס רק אחרי שש שנים מהתשלום הראשון, והמעסיק משלם 7.5% מול 2.5% שלי.

ההשוואה מראה שקרן ההשתלמות משאירה רק 415.84 ₪ יותר אחרי עשר שנים, עם דמי ניהול של 2,402 ₪ לעומת 466 ₪, אם כי המס נמוך יותר; ההפרש עלול גם לצאת שלילי, בין 342.02- ל-2,106 ₪. אני בודק עכשיו את ההנחות של המס.
Screen 4 says the money is free once 6 years pass, and Screen 5 lists fees up to 2% a year with the names אלטשולר שחם, הראל and הפניקס. I'm noting that the 6-year figure repeats across screens.

Screen 6's orange box says early withdrawal is possible but costs 47%, so I'm leaving it alone for six years. The text about trust-held assets with no state guarantee and the screen 7 glossary I skipped; I'm closing it now.

input.answer: It's worth having. My employer puts in 7.5% and I put in 2.5%, and after 6 years from the first payment I can take all of it out tax-free. Before that I can take it out, but it's taxed, up to 47% the page says, so I don't touch it. Only weird part: the calculator says the keren leaves only 415 ₪ more than a regular securities account, which I don't really get.

stuck.why: After 10 years it says the keren leaves only '415.84 ₪ יותר'. That seemed tiny for something everyone calls a great deal, and I'm not sure if that includes the employer's money.
It's on 12,000 gross. I only know my take-home of 9,500 and not my gross, so I left it as it was.
The minus sign made me think the keren can come out worse, and that scared me a bit.
